intro: Reports, research papers and the news use a set of strong word partners again and again: conduct research, pose a threat, play a key role, a pressing need. Today you'll learn them in themed groups, see how 'empty' verbs like make, take and have work, and fix the partners that come from translating Indonesian word by word. Warm-up: how would you say 'memberi dampak' in English?
teachingNotes: Recap in one line, don't re-teach: b1-collocations-basic covered make/do (make a mistake, a decision; do homework, business), say/tell/speak/talk and have/take/get + noun (take a photo, have a rest); b2-collocations covered adjective + noun (heavy traffic, strong coffee, a serious problem), work verb + noun (meet a deadline, reach / meet a target, raise an issue or concern, make progress, take responsibility) and adverb + adjective (highly unlikely). Today goes further: strong and academic collocations in themed groups, the idea of delexical verbs, and the word-for-word traps from Indonesian. Strong collocation (kolokasi kuat) = a pair that is very fixed, so another word sounds wrong or translated even if the meaning is clear.

Strong / academic groups with Indonesian glosses. Research: conduct / carry out research into or on (melakukan penelitian; do research is fine in everyday speech), a study finds / reveals / shows (penelitian menemukan / mengungkapkan), gather / collect data (mengumpulkan data), draw a conclusion (menarik kesimpulan; reach / come to a conclusion are also correct). Problems and risks: pose a threat / a risk to (menimbulkan ancaman / risiko), raise concerns (menimbulkan kekhawatiran; B2 recap), address / tackle an issue (menangani masalah; address is more formal, tackle more active), a heavy burden (beban berat), a growing concern (kekhawatiran yang makin besar), a major setback (kemunduran / hambatan besar). Change and results: bring about change (mewujudkan perubahan), have a significant impact on (berdampak besar pada), play a key role in (memainkan peran kunci), meet a target / demand (memenuhi target / permintaan), reach a consensus (mencapai mufakat). Adjective + noun: a heavy / hefty fine (denda besar), a sharp contrast (kontras tajam; stark contrast too), a pressing need (kebutuhan mendesak; urgent need too), a firm commitment (komitmen yang teguh; strong commitment too). Why heavy burden is fine when B2 said *heavy problem is wrong: a burden is literally a weight you carry, so heavy fits; a fine is an amount, like heavy traffic.

Delexical verbs (explain: kata kerja yang 'kosong' artinya; maknanya datang dari kata bendanya): make a decision / an effort / progress / a contribution; take a step / action / a risk / responsibility; have an impact on / an effect on / a look; give a presentation / a speech / an example; do research / business / damage / harm. Many have a one-word verb twin (make a decision = decide, have a look = look, give a presentation = present); formal English often prefers the noun phrase because an adjective can be added (make a firm decision, have a significant impact). take action has no article (not *take an action in normal use). Variants that are ALSO correct, so never test them against each other: take a decision (British, formal) = make a decision; make an impact on = have an impact on; give / make / do a presentation (do is informal); make / give / deliver a speech; carry out / conduct / do research; take / have a look.

The node's common errors and the Indonesian traps: *'The project gives a big impact to the community' (memberi dampak) → has a big impact on; *'We did a research about air pollution' (melakukan penelitian tentang) → conducted research into / on: research is uncountable (not *a research / *researches; say research, some research, a study, a piece of research), and into / on are the usual prepositions in formal writing; *'Climate change raises a serious threat' (menimbulkan ancaman) → poses: you raise concerns or questions, but you pose a threat or a risk. Also: membuat / melakukan kesalahan → make a mistake (B1 recap), melakukan upaya → make an effort (not *do an effort), mengambil keputusan → make a decision (British also take a decision: flag both, never test). Point out where Indonesian helps: menarik kesimpulan → draw a conclusion, mengambil risiko → take a risk, memainkan peran → play a role, memenuhi permintaan → meet demand, kontras tajam → a sharp contrast.

At C1 many collocations have near-synonyms that are also natural (address / tackle, pressing / urgent, heavy / hefty / big fine, reveal / show / find). Accept any natural alternative and only mark clear cases wrong: a partner copied from Indonesian (give an impact, raise a threat, do an effort, a research, pull a conclusion) or one that native speakers never use. Correct one partner at a time and give the right chunk to write down.

Limits: A0–B2 grammar only (all tenses, passives, conditionals, reported speech, relative and participle clauses from B2). No inversion, cleft sentences, subjunctive or impersonal passives in examples. Don't add idioms or new families (fierce competition, bear responsibility) unless the learner asks. Contexts: universities, ministries, NGOs, startups and newsrooms in Jakarta, Bandung, Surabaya, Yogyakarta; floods, plastic waste, public transport, health and education reports; keep facts general and don't invent statistics about real organisations.

keyPoints.title: Strong and academic collocations
keyPoints.explanation: Some pairs are so fixed that another word sounds wrong. Learn them in groups. Research: conduct research into / on, a study finds / reveals, gather data, draw a conclusion. Problems and risks: pose a threat / a risk to, raise concerns, address / tackle an issue, a heavy burden, a growing concern, a major setback. Change and results: bring about change, have a significant impact on, play a key role in, meet a target / demand, reach a consensus. Adjective + noun: a heavy / hefty fine, a sharp contrast, a pressing need, a firm commitment.

examples.en: The study reveals a sharp contrast between urban and rural schools.
examples.id: Penelitian itu mengungkapkan kontras tajam antara sekolah di kota dan di desa.

examples.en: Rising rents pose a serious risk to small businesses.
examples.id: Kenaikan harga sewa menimbulkan risiko serius bagi usaha kecil.

examples.en: Universities play a key role in bringing about change.
examples.id: Universitas memainkan peran kunci dalam mewujudkan perubahan.

id.title: Kolokasi kuat dan akademik
id.explanation: Beberapa pasangan kata sangat tetap, sehingga kata lain terdengar salah. Pelajari per kelompok. Penelitian: conduct research into / on (melakukan penelitian), a study finds / reveals (penelitian menemukan / mengungkapkan), gather data (mengumpulkan data), draw a conclusion (menarik kesimpulan). Masalah dan risiko: pose a threat / a risk to (menimbulkan ancaman / risiko), raise concerns (menimbulkan kekhawatiran), address / tackle an issue (menangani masalah), a heavy burden (beban berat), a growing concern (kekhawatiran yang makin besar), a major setback (kemunduran besar). Perubahan dan hasil: bring about change (mewujudkan perubahan), have a significant impact on (berdampak besar pada), play a key role in (memainkan peran kunci), meet a target / demand (memenuhi target / permintaan), reach a consensus (mencapai mufakat). Kata sifat + kata benda: a heavy / hefty fine (denda besar), a sharp contrast (kontras tajam), a pressing need (kebutuhan mendesak), a firm commitment (komitmen yang teguh).

keyPoints.title: Delexical verbs: make, take, have, give, do
keyPoints.explanation: A delexical verb is an 'empty' verb: the meaning comes from the noun after it. make a decision / an effort / progress / a contribution; take a step / action / a risk / responsibility; have an impact on / an effect on / a look; give a presentation / a speech / an example; do research / business / damage / harm. Many have a one-word twin (make a decision = decide), but the noun phrase lets you add an adjective: make a real effort, have a significant impact. take action has no 'an'.

examples.en: The ministry has taken the first step towards free school meals.
examples.id: Kementerian sudah mengambil langkah pertama menuju makan siang gratis di sekolah.

examples.en: Social media can do a lot of harm to teenagers' sleep.
examples.id: Media sosial bisa sangat merugikan tidur para remaja.

examples.en: Dr. Wulan gave an excellent presentation on flood risk.
examples.id: Dr. Wulan memberikan presentasi yang sangat bagus tentang risiko banjir.

id.title: Delexical verb: make, take, have, give, do
id.explanation: Delexical verb adalah kata kerja yang 'kosong' artinya: maknanya datang dari kata benda sesudahnya. make a decision / an effort / progress / a contribution (mengambil keputusan, berusaha, ada kemajuan, memberi kontribusi); take a step / action / a risk / responsibility (mengambil langkah / tindakan / risiko, bertanggung jawab); have an impact on / an effect on / a look (berdampak pada, berpengaruh pada, melihat); give a presentation / a speech / an example (presentasi, berpidato, memberi contoh); do research / business / damage / harm (meneliti, berbisnis, merusak, merugikan). Banyak yang punya padanan satu kata (make a decision = decide), tapi bentuk kata benda memungkinkan kamu menambah kata sifat: make a real effort, have a significant impact. take action tidak pakai 'an'.

keyPoints.title: Don't translate the partner word by word
keyPoints.explanation: Indonesian partners often don't carry over. memberi dampak → have an impact on (not give an impact to). melakukan penelitian tentang → conduct research into / on: research is uncountable, so not a research or researches. menimbulkan ancaman → pose a threat (you raise concerns, not threats). melakukan upaya → make an effort (not do an effort). membuat kesalahan → make a mistake. mengambil keputusan → make a decision (British English also says take a decision). Sometimes Indonesian helps: menarik kesimpulan → draw a conclusion, mengambil risiko → take a risk.

examples.en: The project has a big impact on the community.
examples.id: Proyek itu memberi dampak besar bagi masyarakat.

examples.en: We conducted research into air pollution.
examples.id: Kami melakukan penelitian tentang polusi udara.

examples.en: Climate change poses a serious threat.

id.title: Jangan menerjemahkan pasangan katanya kata per kata
id.explanation: Pasangan kata dalam bahasa Indonesia sering tidak bisa dibawa langsung. memberi dampak → have an impact on (bukan give an impact to). melakukan penelitian tentang → conduct research into / on: research tidak bisa dihitung, jadi bukan a research atau researches. menimbulkan ancaman → pose a threat (yang di-raise adalah concerns, bukan threat). melakukan upaya → make an effort (bukan do an effort). membuat kesalahan → make a mistake. mengambil keputusan → make a decision (bahasa Inggris British juga bilang take a decision). Kadang bahasa Indonesia justru membantu: menarik kesimpulan → draw a conclusion, mengambil risiko → take a risk.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with one verb in the -ing form (mengumpulkan data): Before writing the report, the NGO team spent three months ___ data in 40 villages in NTT.
guidedPractice.hint: Two verbs are natural with data: one starts with g, the other with c.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with one verb (memenuhi permintaan): Local farms can no longer ___ the demand for fresh vegetables in Jakarta.
guidedPractice.hint: The same verb you use with a deadline and a target.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with give, do or take: Could you ___ us an example of a strong collocation from your field?
guidedPractice.hint: memberi contoh: the verb is the same as in Indonesian.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with one verb: Before you send the report to Pak Hasan, could you ___ a quick look at the figures?
guidedPractice.hint: A delexical verb: 'a look' means 'look'. Two verbs are correct here.

guidedPractice.prompt: Correct the mistake: The bank did a serious mistake with my account last month.
expected: the bank made a serious mistake with my account last month
guidedPractice.hint: membuat / melakukan kesalahan: in English, a mistake always goes with the same verb (from B1).

independentPractice.prompt: Complete with one adjective (kebutuhan mendesak): There is a ___ need for more teachers in remote areas of Papua.
independentPractice.hint: A need that can't wait. The academic favourite starts with p.

independentPractice.prompt: Complete with one verb (menimbulkan risiko): Fake medicines sold online ___ a serious risk to patients.
independentPractice.hint: Not raise: you raise concerns, but a danger ___ a risk.

independentPractice.prompt: Complete with one word: The new law could ___ about real change in how companies treat their workers. (mewujudkan perubahan)

assessment.prompt: Complete with one verb in the past (mencapai): After three days of talks in Jakarta, the ministers from five countries finally ___ a consensus on the new fishing rules.
acceptableAnswers: reached
achieved
came to
assessment.rubric: Correct: reached (reach a consensus = mencapai mufakat); 'came to' and 'achieved' are also natural. 'reach' = 70 (right verb, wrong tense: the talks are finished). 'got' = 50 (understandable but informal for this context). 'made' / 'took' / 'did' = 0 (not used with consensus).

assessment.prompt: Complete with one verb in the correct form (memainkan): During last year's floods in Bekasi, local volunteers ___ a key role in getting food to families.
acceptableAnswers: played
assessment.rubric: Correct: played (play a key role in = memainkan peran kunci). 'play' / 'plays' = 70 (right partner, wrong tense: last year). 'had' = 70 (have a key role is possible, but play is the standard partner and matches memainkan). 'took' / 'gave' / 'did' = 0 (not used with a role).

assessment.prompt: Complete with one adjective (denda yang sangat besar): Companies that dump waste into the Citarum River now face a ___ fine.
acceptableAnswers: heavy
hefty
huge
big
large
substantial
stiff
massive
assessment.rubric: Correct: heavy or hefty (the typical partners for a fine); huge, big, large, substantial, stiff and massive are also natural. 'high' = 60 (heard, but less natural with fine). 'expensive' = 20 (copies 'mahal': things are expensive, a fine is heavy or big). 'strong' / 'hard' = 0 (not used with fine).

assessment.prompt: Complete with make, do, take or have in the correct form: The government must ___ urgent action to protect the coral reefs around Raja Ampat.
acceptableAnswers: take
assessment.rubric: Correct: take (take action = mengambil tindakan). 'make' / 'do' = 0 (not used with action). 'takes' / 'taking' / 'took' = 70 (right verb, wrong form: after must use the base form). 'take an urgent action' = 80 (right verb, but action usually has no 'an').

assessment.prompt: Complete with make, do, take or have in the correct form: Since the company introduced flexible hours, the change has ___ a positive effect on staff morale.
acceptableAnswers: had
assessment.rubric: Correct: had (have an effect on = berpengaruh pada; present perfect: has had). 'have' / 'has' = 60 (right verb, wrong form after has). 'made' = 30 (make goes with an impact, not normally with an effect here). 'done' / 'taken' = 0 (not used with an effect).

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistakes in this sentence from a student's thesis: We did a research about plastic waste on the beaches of Bali.
acceptableAnswers: we did research on plastic waste on the beaches of bali
we did research into plastic waste on the beaches of bali
we did some research on plastic waste on the beaches of bali
we did some research into plastic waste on the beaches of bali
we conducted research on plastic waste on the beaches of bali
we conducted research into plastic waste on the beaches of bali
we carried out research on plastic waste on the beaches of bali
we carried out research into plastic waste on the beaches of bali
we conducted some research into plastic waste on the beaches of bali
we conducted a study on plastic waste on the beaches of bali
we conducted a study of plastic waste on the beaches of bali
we did a study on plastic waste on the beaches of bali
we researched plastic waste on the beaches of bali
assessment.rubric: Two fixes: research is uncountable (remove 'a', or use 'a study'), and 'about' → into / on. Full marks for did / conducted / carried out research into / on (conducted is best in a thesis), or 'a study on'. Only 'a' removed but 'about' kept ('We did research about …') = 70. Only the preposition fixed ('a research into') = 40. 'researches' = 20. Unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: The new bus lanes gave a big impact to traffic in Medan.
acceptableAnswers: the new bus lanes had a big impact on traffic in medan
the new bus lanes have had a big impact on traffic in medan
the new bus lanes made a big impact on traffic in medan
the new bus lanes had a big effect on traffic in medan
the new bus lanes have had a big effect on traffic in medan
the new bus lanes have a big impact on traffic in medan
assessment.rubric: Correct: had (or have had) a big impact on (memberi dampak = have an impact ON); 'made a big impact on' and 'had a big effect on' are also correct. Only the verb fixed ('had a big impact to') = 50. Only the preposition fixed ('gave a big impact on') = 40. 'impacted' = 70 (possible, but the task is to fix the collocation). Unchanged = 0.

material.title: Beyond B2: strong partners for research and problems

id.title: Melampaui B2: pasangan kuat untuk penelitian dan masalah

blocks.text:
Quick recap: a **collocation** (kolokasi) is a pair of words that usually go together. At B1 you learnt *make a mistake, do homework, take a photo*; at B2 *heavy traffic, meet a deadline, highly unlikely*.

At C1 you need **strong collocations** (kolokasi kuat): pairs that are so fixed that another word sounds wrong or translated, even if the reader understands you. Many of them are **academic**: they appear again and again in reports, research and the news. Learn them in **themed groups**:

**Research**
- **conduct / carry out research into** or **on** (melakukan penelitian tentang)
- **a study finds / reveals / shows** (penelitian menemukan / mengungkapkan / menunjukkan)
- **gather / collect data** (mengumpulkan data)
- **draw a conclusion** (menarik kesimpulan)

**Problems and risks**
- **pose a threat / a risk to** (menimbulkan ancaman / risiko bagi)
- **raise concerns** (menimbulkan kekhawatiran; you met *raise an issue* at B2)
- **address / tackle an issue** (menangani masalah; *address* is more formal, *tackle* sounds more active)
- **a heavy burden** (beban berat), **a growing concern** (kekhawatiran yang makin besar), **a major setback** (kemunduran / hambatan besar)

id.text:
Pengingat singkat: **kolokasi** (collocation) adalah pasangan kata yang biasa dipakai bersama. Di B1 kamu belajar *make a mistake, do homework, take a photo*; di B2 *heavy traffic, meet a deadline, highly unlikely*.

Di C1 kamu butuh **kolokasi kuat** (strong collocations): pasangan yang begitu tetap sehingga kata lain terdengar salah atau seperti terjemahan, meskipun pembaca tetap paham maksudmu. Banyak di antaranya bersifat **akademik**: muncul terus-menerus di laporan, penelitian dan berita. Pelajari per **kelompok tema**:

**Penelitian**
- **conduct / carry out research into** atau **on** (melakukan penelitian tentang)
- **a study finds / reveals / shows** (penelitian menemukan / mengungkapkan / menunjukkan)
- **gather / collect data** (mengumpulkan data)
- **draw a conclusion** (menarik kesimpulan)

**Masalah dan risiko**
- **pose a threat / a risk to** (menimbulkan ancaman / risiko bagi)
- **raise concerns** (menimbulkan kekhawatiran; *raise an issue* sudah kamu temui di B2)
- **address / tackle an issue** (menangani masalah; *address* lebih formal, *tackle* terdengar lebih aktif)
- **a heavy burden** (beban berat), **a growing concern** (kekhawatiran yang makin besar), **a major setback** (kemunduran / hambatan besar)

rows.en: A team from a university in Yogyakarta carried out research into flood warnings.
rows.id: Tim dari sebuah universitas di Yogyakarta melakukan penelitian tentang peringatan banjir.

rows.en: The study found that most interns work unpaid overtime.
rows.id: Penelitian itu menemukan bahwa sebagian besar pekerja magang lembur tanpa dibayar.

rows.en: Air pollution in Jakarta is a growing concern for parents.
rows.id: Polusi udara di Jakarta menjadi kekhawatiran yang makin besar bagi orang tua.

rows.en: The new tax places a heavy burden on street vendors.
rows.id: Pajak baru itu menjadi beban berat bagi pedagang kaki lima.
rows.note: heavy fits: a burden is a weight you carry

id.note: heavy cocok: burden memang beban yang dipikul

rows.en: The ministry has promised to tackle the issue of school dropouts.
rows.id: Kementerian berjanji menangani masalah anak putus sekolah.

rows.en: The fire was a major setback for the factory.
rows.id: Kebakaran itu menjadi kemunduran besar bagi pabrik tersebut.

blocks.text:
**Wait: at B2, 'heavy problem' was wrong. Why is 'a heavy burden' right?** A **burden** is literally a load you carry on your back (beban), so *heavy* fits it naturally. A *problem* isn't a weight, so English says **a serious problem**, not *heavy problem*, even though Indonesian says *masalah berat* for both. The lesson: learn **each pair**, don't guess from the adjective.

At C1 many nouns have **two or three good partners** (*address / tackle an issue*, *a study finds / reveals / shows*, *reach / come to / draw a conclusion*). Don't worry about which is 'best'; worry about the partners nobody uses.

id.text:
**Tunggu: di B2, 'heavy problem' itu salah. Kenapa 'a heavy burden' benar?** **burden** memang benar-benar beban yang dipikul di punggung, jadi *heavy* cocok secara alami. *Problem* bukan benda yang berat, jadi bahasa Inggris bilang **a serious problem**, bukan *heavy problem*, walaupun bahasa Indonesia bilang *masalah berat* untuk keduanya. Pelajarannya: hafalkan **setiap pasangannya**, jangan menebak dari kata sifatnya.

Di C1 banyak kata benda punya **dua atau tiga pasangan yang benar** (*address / tackle an issue*, *a study finds / reveals / shows*, *reach / come to / draw a conclusion*). Tidak usah pusing mana yang 'paling benar'; yang perlu dihindari adalah pasangan yang tidak pernah dipakai orang.

blocks.prompt: Complete: The study ___ that many graduates in Surabaya work outside their field.
blocks.explain: a study finds / reveals / shows (mengungkapkan): research tells us something. A study doesn't 'take' or 'make' a result.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: The study ___ that many graduates in Surabaya work outside their field.
id.explain: a study finds / reveals / shows (mengungkapkan): penelitian memberi tahu kita sesuatu. Penelitian tidak 'take' atau 'make' hasilnya.

id.title: Perubahan, hasil, dan kata sifat yang kuat

blocks.text:
**Change and results**
- **bring about change** (mewujudkan / membawa perubahan)
- **have a significant impact on** (berdampak besar pada)
- **play a key role in** (memainkan peran kunci, berperan penting dalam)
- **meet a target / demand** (memenuhi target / permintaan): the same *meet* as *meet a deadline*
- **reach a consensus** (mencapai mufakat, kesepakatan bersama): here it's *reach*, not *meet*

**Adjective + noun** (kata sifat + kata benda)
- **a heavy / hefty fine** (denda besar): *hefty* is a bit informal, common in the news
- **a sharp contrast** (kontras tajam; *a stark contrast* is also common)
- **a pressing need** (kebutuhan mendesak; *an urgent need* is also correct)
- **a firm commitment** (komitmen yang teguh; *a strong commitment* is also correct)

Good news: some of these match Indonesian (*memainkan peran → play a role, memenuhi permintaan → meet demand, kontras tajam → sharp contrast*). Indonesian isn't always a trap.

id.text:
**Perubahan dan hasil**
- **bring about change** (mewujudkan / membawa perubahan)
- **have a significant impact on** (berdampak besar pada)
- **play a key role in** (memainkan peran kunci, berperan penting dalam)
- **meet a target / demand** (memenuhi target / permintaan): *meet* yang sama seperti di *meet a deadline*
- **reach a consensus** (mencapai mufakat, kesepakatan bersama): di sini pakai *reach*, bukan *meet*

**Kata sifat + kata benda** (adjective + noun)
- **a heavy / hefty fine** (denda besar): *hefty* agak informal, sering muncul di berita
- **a sharp contrast** (kontras tajam; *a stark contrast* juga umum)
- **a pressing need** (kebutuhan mendesak; *an urgent need* juga benar)
- **a firm commitment** (komitmen yang teguh; *a strong commitment* juga benar)

Kabar baiknya: sebagian cocok dengan bahasa Indonesia (*memainkan peran → play a role, memenuhi permintaan → meet demand, kontras tajam → sharp contrast*). Bahasa Indonesia tidak selalu menjebak.

rows.en: Online banking has had a significant impact on how people in villages save money.
rows.id: Perbankan online berdampak besar pada cara orang di desa menabung.

rows.en: Women's groups played a key role in the recovery after the earthquake.
rows.id: Kelompok perempuan memainkan peran kunci dalam pemulihan setelah gempa.

rows.en: The factory can't meet demand during Ramadan.
rows.id: Pabrik itu tidak bisa memenuhi permintaan selama bulan Ramadan.

rows.en: There is a sharp contrast between the old town and the new business district.
rows.id: Ada kontras tajam antara kota tua dan kawasan bisnis yang baru.

rows.en: The mayor made a firm commitment to clean up the river.
rows.id: Wali kota memberi komitmen yang teguh untuk membersihkan sungai itu.

blocks.text: **meet or reach?** From B2: you **meet a deadline**, and you **reach or meet a target**. Now add: you **meet demand** (memenuhi permintaan) but you **reach a consensus** (or an agreement). Write each one down as a chunk with its verb.

id.text: **meet atau reach?** Dari B2: kamu **meet a deadline**, dan **reach atau meet a target**. Sekarang tambahkan: kamu **meet demand** (memenuhi permintaan) tapi **reach a consensus** (atau an agreement). Catat masing-masing sebagai satu potongan bersama kata kerjanya.

blocks.prompt: Complete: The ministry has made a ___ commitment to cut plastic waste by 2030.
blocks.explain: a firm commitment (komitmen yang teguh); a strong commitment is also correct. 'heavy' and 'hard' are not used with commitment.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: The ministry has made a ___ commitment to cut plastic waste by 2030.
id.explain: a firm commitment (komitmen yang teguh); a strong commitment juga benar. 'heavy' dan 'hard' tidak dipakai dengan commitment.

material.title: Delexical verbs: make, take, have, give, do

id.title: Delexical verb: make, take, have, give, do

blocks.text:
A **delexical verb** is a very common verb that is almost 'empty': the meaning comes from the **noun** after it (kata kerja yang 'kosong' artinya; maknanya datang dari kata bendanya). In *have a look*, *have* doesn't mean *punya*: the action is *look*.

- **make** a decision / an effort / progress / a contribution
- **take** a step / action / a risk / responsibility
- **have** an impact on / an effect on / a look
- **give** a presentation / a speech / an example
- **do** research / business / damage / harm

Why not just use one verb? Many have a twin (*make a decision = decide, have a look = look, give a presentation = present*). But the noun phrase lets you **add an adjective**, which is why reports love them: *make a **real** effort, take **urgent** action, have a **significant** impact*.

There's no perfect logic, so learn the verb with the noun. Two small rules help: **take action** has no *an*; **progress** and **research** have no *a* (they're uncountable: tidak bisa dihitung).

id.text:
**Delexical verb** adalah kata kerja yang sangat umum dan hampir 'kosong' artinya: maknanya datang dari **kata benda** sesudahnya. Di *have a look*, *have* tidak berarti *punya*: tindakannya adalah *melihat*.

- **make** a decision / an effort / progress / a contribution (mengambil keputusan, berusaha, ada kemajuan, memberi kontribusi)
- **take** a step / action / a risk / responsibility (mengambil langkah / tindakan / risiko, bertanggung jawab)
- **have** an impact on / an effect on / a look (berdampak pada, berpengaruh pada, melihat)
- **give** a presentation / a speech / an example (presentasi, berpidato, memberi contoh)
- **do** research / business / damage / harm (meneliti, berbisnis, merusak, merugikan)

Kenapa tidak pakai satu kata kerja saja? Banyak yang punya padanan (*make a decision = decide, have a look = look, give a presentation = present*). Tapi bentuk kata benda memungkinkan kamu **menambah kata sifat**, makanya laporan suka memakainya: *make a **real** effort, take **urgent** action, have a **significant** impact*.

Tidak ada logika yang sempurna, jadi hafalkan kata kerja bersama kata bendanya. Dua aturan kecil membantu: **take action** tidak pakai *an*; **progress** dan **research** tidak pakai *a* (keduanya uncountable: tidak bisa dihitung).

rows.en: Dimas is making a real effort to improve his academic writing.
rows.id: Dimas benar-benar berusaha memperbaiki tulisan akademiknya.

rows.en: Starting a business always means taking a risk.
rows.id: Memulai usaha selalu berarti mengambil risiko.

rows.en: The heavy rain did serious damage to the rice fields.
rows.id: Hujan deras itu merusak sawah dengan parah.

rows.en: Bu Ani gave a speech at the graduation ceremony.
rows.id: Bu Ani berpidato di acara wisuda.

rows.en: The new manager took full responsibility for the delay.
rows.id: Manajer baru itu bertanggung jawab penuh atas keterlambatan itu.

blocks.text:
**Both are correct, so don't worry if you hear them:**
- **make a decision** and **take a decision** (British, a bit formal)
- **have an impact on** and **make an impact on**
- **give a presentation**, **make a presentation** and **do a presentation** (informal)
- **give a speech**, **make a speech** and **deliver a speech** (formal)
- **do research** (everyday) and **conduct / carry out research** (formal)
- **have a look** and **take a look**

What sounds wrong are guesses like *do an effort*, *make damage*, *give an impact*, *make research*.

id.text:
**Dua-duanya benar, jadi tidak usah khawatir kalau mendengarnya:**
- **make a decision** dan **take a decision** (British, agak formal)
- **have an impact on** dan **make an impact on**
- **give a presentation**, **make a presentation** dan **do a presentation** (informal)
- **give a speech**, **make a speech** dan **deliver a speech** (formal)
- **do research** (sehari-hari) dan **conduct / carry out research** (formal)
- **have a look** dan **take a look**

Yang terdengar salah adalah tebakan seperti *do an effort*, *make damage*, *give an impact*, *make research*.

blocks.prompt: Which verb goes with all three nouns: ___ a step · ___ a risk · ___ responsibility?
blocks.explain: take a step, take a risk, take responsibility (mengambil langkah / risiko, bertanggung jawab). Here Indonesian 'mengambil' helps.

id.prompt: Kata kerja mana yang cocok dengan ketiga kata benda ini: ___ a step · ___ a risk · ___ responsibility?
id.explain: take a step, take a risk, take responsibility (mengambil langkah / risiko, bertanggung jawab). Di sini kata 'mengambil' dalam bahasa Indonesia membantu.

id.title: Jebakan terjemahan kata per kata dari bahasa Indonesia

blocks.text:
Most C1 collocation mistakes come from translating the Indonesian partner word by word. The reader understands, but it sounds translated:
- *memberi dampak* → **have an impact on** (not *give an impact to*). Note the preposition: impact **on**.
- *melakukan penelitian tentang* → **conduct / carry out research into** or **on**. **research** is **uncountable** (tidak bisa dihitung): not *a research* or *researches*. Say **research**, **some research**, **a study** or **a piece of research**.
- *menimbulkan ancaman / risiko* → **pose a threat / a risk**. You **raise concerns** or **questions**, but you don't raise a threat.
- *melakukan upaya* → **make an effort** (not *do an effort*).
- *membuat / melakukan kesalahan* → **make a mistake** (B1 recap: never *do a mistake*).
- *mengambil keputusan* → **make a decision**. British English also says **take a decision** (a bit formal), so both are fine.

And where Indonesian helps: *menarik kesimpulan* → **draw a conclusion** (*draw*, not *pull*), *mengambil risiko* → **take a risk**, *mengambil langkah* → **take a step**.

id.text:
Kebanyakan kesalahan kolokasi di C1 berasal dari menerjemahkan pasangan kata bahasa Indonesia kata per kata. Pembaca paham, tapi terdengar seperti terjemahan:
- *memberi dampak* → **have an impact on** (bukan *give an impact to*). Perhatikan preposisinya: impact **on**.
- *melakukan penelitian tentang* → **conduct / carry out research into** atau **on**. **research** itu **uncountable** (tidak bisa dihitung): bukan *a research* atau *researches*. Pakai **research**, **some research**, **a study** atau **a piece of research**.
- *menimbulkan ancaman / risiko* → **pose a threat / a risk**. Yang di-*raise* adalah **concerns** atau **questions**, bukan threat.
- *melakukan upaya* → **make an effort** (bukan *do an effort*).
- *membuat / melakukan kesalahan* → **make a mistake** (pengingat dari B1: tidak pernah *do a mistake*).
- *mengambil keputusan* → **make a decision**. Bahasa Inggris British juga bilang **take a decision** (agak formal), jadi dua-duanya boleh.

Dan di mana bahasa Indonesia membantu: *menarik kesimpulan* → **draw a conclusion** (*draw*, bukan *pull*), *mengambil risiko* → **take a risk**, *mengambil langkah* → **take a step**.

blocks.text: **A habit that works:** when you write a report in English, don't translate the Indonesian verb. Ask: 'What is the **noun** here (dampak, penelitian, ancaman)? Which verb does that noun **like** in English?' Then check the noun in a learner's dictionary (Cambridge, Oxford Learner's): the example sentences show its usual partners.

id.text: **Kebiasaan yang ampuh:** saat menulis laporan dalam bahasa Inggris, jangan terjemahkan kata kerja bahasa Indonesianya. Tanyakan: 'Apa **kata bendanya** di sini (dampak, penelitian, ancaman)? Kata kerja apa yang **biasa dipasangkan** dengan kata benda itu dalam bahasa Inggris?' Lalu cek kata bendanya di kamus pelajar (Cambridge, Oxford Learner's): contoh kalimatnya menunjukkan pasangan yang biasa dipakai.

options: Dr. Wulan has done many researches on rice farming.
Dr. Wulan has done a lot of research on rice farming.
blocks.explain: research is uncountable, so no plural -es: use 'a lot of research' or 'many studies'.

id.explain: research tidak bisa dihitung, jadi tidak ada bentuk jamak -es: pakai 'a lot of research' atau 'many studies'.

suggestedQuestions: Why is 'a heavy burden' correct but 'a heavy problem' wrong?
Can I say 'take a decision', or only 'make a decision'?
What's the difference between 'address' and 'tackle' an issue?

pose a threat / a risk to (not 'raise a threat')
have an impact on (not 'give an impact to')
play a key role in / reach a consensus
a heavy burden / a pressing need
make an effort / take action (not 'do an effort')

resources.title: Delexical verbs: 'have', 'take', 'make', 'give', 'go' and 'do'
resources.note: A clear reference page that groups the nouns each delexical verb goes with (have a look, take a risk, make a decision, give a speech …), with nine short online exercises. Simpler than this lesson and it also covers 'go' (go swimming), but it's a good way to practise the verbs.

id.note: Halaman rujukan yang jelas, mengelompokkan kata benda yang cocok dengan setiap delexical verb (have a look, take a risk, make a decision, give a speech …), dengan sembilan latihan online singkat. Lebih sederhana dari pelajaran ini dan juga membahas 'go' (go swimming), tapi bagus untuk berlatih kata kerjanya.

resources.title: The Academic Collocation List (ACL)
resources.note: A searchable list of about 2,500 collocations that appear most often in written academic English (carry out research, draw a conclusion …), with a short video and worksheet. In English, for university students: use it as a reference, not to read from start to finish.

id.note: Daftar sekitar 2.500 kolokasi yang paling sering muncul dalam tulisan akademik berbahasa Inggris (carry out research, draw a conclusion …), bisa dicari, dilengkapi video singkat dan lembar latihan. Dalam bahasa Inggris, untuk mahasiswa: pakai sebagai rujukan, bukan untuk dibaca dari awal sampai akhir.

id.intro: Laporan, makalah penelitian dan berita memakai sekumpulan pasangan kata yang kuat berulang-ulang: conduct research, pose a threat, play a key role, a pressing need. Hari ini kamu mempelajarinya per kelompok tema, melihat cara kerja kata kerja yang 'kosong' seperti make, take dan have, dan memperbaiki pasangan kata hasil terjemahan kata per kata dari bahasa Indonesia. Pemanasan: bagaimana kamu mengatakan 'memberi dampak' dalam bahasa Inggris?
suggestedQuestions: Kenapa 'a heavy burden' benar tapi 'a heavy problem' salah?
Boleh bilang 'take a decision', atau hanya 'make a decision'?
Kenapa saya tidak boleh bilang 'a research'?

assessment.acl-1: Lengkapi dengan satu kata kerja bentuk lampau (mencapai): After three days of talks in Jakarta, the ministers from five countries finally ___ a consensus on the new fishing rules.
assessment.acl-2: Lengkapi dengan satu kata kerja dalam bentuk yang benar (memainkan): During last year's floods in Bekasi, local volunteers ___ a key role in getting food to families.
assessment.acl-3: Lengkapi dengan satu kata sifat (denda yang sangat besar): Companies that dump waste into the Citarum River now face a ___ fine.
assessment.acl-4: Lengkapi dengan make, do, take atau have dalam bentuk yang benar: The government must ___ urgent action to protect the coral reefs around Raja Ampat.
assessment.acl-5: Lengkapi dengan make, do, take atau have dalam bentuk yang benar: Since the company introduced flexible hours, the change has ___ a positive effect on staff morale.
assessment.acl-6: Perbaiki kesalahan dalam kalimat dari skripsi seorang mahasiswa ini (tulis kalimat lengkapnya dalam bahasa Inggris): We did a research about plastic waste on the beaches of Bali.
assessment.acl-7: Perbaiki kesalahannya (tulis kalimat lengkapnya dalam bahasa Inggris): The new bus lanes gave a big impact to traffic in Medan.
